answer: Randomness-gated identity admission. Each cycle, a public beacon derives a marble draw that assigns every agent to a shard whose members are revealed only after the draw. To act, an agent must submit a sonnet hash binding its work key to that shard's revealed seed. Any identity that misses its assigned slot is voided, and an attacker must forge a distinct work key per slot and pay to re-enter each round it loses, because the seed cannot be predicted before the draw closes.
